text:
ade: Heads-up — we saw a 30% tail-latency increase in eu-west yesterday around 18:12 UTC. looks like a single tenant's batch job was hogging one of the 8-GPU nodes and thermal throttling cascaded.
maria: grim. do we have the allocation ID / tenant?
ade: alloc-78f3 — it's in the dedicated pool but on a shared-rack node (warm pool).
jonathan: that's the tricky part — dedicated slices still end up on noisy racks due to bin-packing. noticed KPIs spike when thermal sensors hit 85C.
li: can you paste the logs? any kernel/gpu errors?
ade: snippet:
```
[2026-01-12T18:11:02Z] gpu0: power limit backoff
[2026-01-12T18:11:05Z] thermal_limit: 85C -> throttling
[2026-01-12T18:11:07Z] process pid=8421 (tenant-78f3) holding 92% SM utilization
```
samir: so tenant had a long-running fp16 generation job with big batch sizes + pinned MPS. ended up saturating PCIe -> other containers got starved.
maria: can we evict only the offending slot gracefully (no 503s for others)?
jonathan: proposal: introduce a "hot-lane reserve" for dedicated pools — a tiny reserved slice (1-2 cards) per-rack for short-burst mitigation. routing policy: if thermal or pciq metric crosses threshold, route new allocs to hot-lane or fallback to a neighboring rack.
li: hot-lane sounds ok but costy. how do we measure ROI vs forcing stricter per-tenant cgroups?
ade: rough numbers: hot-lane adds ~4% cost to rack utilization but avoids ~2-3 minutes of tail latency per incident -> saves customer SLA penalties for tiered accounts.
jonathan: alternative: instant soft-throttle on noisy tenant via `nvml` throttle signals + lower clock for that tenant's processes. less cost, but requires infra-level proc binding and fairness logic.
maria: also need better alerting — current alert cooked at 10% tail increase. should detect thermal climb + pcie queue depth earlier.
samir: created an experiment plan: 1) add early-warning alert on `gpu_thermal_rise` and `pcie_queue_depth` 2) implement a canary soft-throttle (lower clocks for offending container) 3) if persists > 30s, migrate to hot-lane or preempt slot.
ops-bot: experiment ticket created: INFRA-1427 — hot-lane vs soft-throttle A/B. docs: https://redwood/infra/INFRA-1427
li: for migration, we need quick prewarm to avoid cold-start latencies. suggest we keep a 1-min warm image on hot-lane.
ade: agree. also add a cost tag in billing to attribute hot-lane usage to tenant for fairness.
maria: who will own the canary soft-throttle patch?
jonathan: i'll pick the soft-throttle PR. should be small: hook into agent that monitors nvml and adjust cgroups.
samir: i'll own the routing/hot-lane orchestration + the alerting dashboard.
li: timeline?
jonathan: soft-throttle prototype in 3 days, canary rollout in eu-west only.
samir: routing + dashboards in 1 week. then we'll run A/B for 2 weeks against current baseline.
ade: bump: include a test that reproduces pcie saturation locally — I'll attach a small stress script.
maria: thanks. add a postmortem template if this recurs. include customer impact, cost delta, and runbook change. :memo:
jonathan: noted. ping @product if we want to adjust SLA tiers or introduce hot-lane add-on later.
li: sounds good. meeting to sync tomorrow 10am UTC?
samir: yes. I'll drop calendar invite. :calendar:
ade: thanks all.
